title: Is it a sin?
hookLine: tattoos, a drink, a bet: the questions people actually search, and Paul's way of thinking about them
last: THE FIRST DAY, A NEW START.

lines: A SEARCH BAR, LATE AT NIGHT.
cards: Late at night, a search bar. Is it a sin to get a tattoo. To drink.
To bet on the game. The questions people type are rarely about the creeds. They're about Saturday night, and skin, and money.
Online answers come fast, certain, and contradictory. The first Christians had their own versions. Could you eat meat that had been offered to an idol?
Did one holy day matter more than another? Paul got questions like these in letters, and his answer wasn't a list but a way of thinking. Today's word is its name.

teach.b: Adiaphora. Greek for things indifferent: not commanded, not forbidden. Stoic philosophers used the word, and in the 1500s Lutheran reformers made it a church word for matters left to conscience.

teach.h: FULLY PERSUADED IN HIS OWN MIND.
teach.b: He tells the church in Rome to welcome one another, "but not to doubtful disputations," and on holy days he says, in the King James Bible: "Let every man be fully persuaded in his own mind."
To another church: "All things are lawful for me, but all things are not expedient." Allowed isn't the same as helpful. Where the line falls, churches honestly differ.
Tattoos: an old law of Moses says, "nor print any marks upon you." Many Christians read it as part of ancient Israel's mourning and worship laws; some avoid tattoos because of it.
Coptic Christians in Egypt have long tattooed a small cross on the wrist.
Alcohol: Jesus turned water into wine at a wedding, and a letter of Paul's says, "be not drunk with wine."

Catholics, Orthodox, Lutherans and Anglicans use wine at communion; many Baptist, Pentecostal and Methodist churches have asked members not to drink, and serve grape juice. Gambling: the Bible never names it.
The United Methodist Church opposes it; the Catholic catechism says games of chance aren't wrong in themselves, but become wrong when they take what someone needs.
Sex and dating are a bigger conversation, and a later one.
Under all of it, Paul adds a rule about the other person: "judge this rather, that no man put a stumblingblock or an occasion to fall in his brother's way." Be persuaded.
Then be kind to the person who lands somewhere else.

how: Christians usually take questions like tattoos, drinking or gambling to their church's teaching, their pastor or priest, and their own conscience. Churches answer them differently, and many point to Paul's advice in Romans 14 not to judge one another over disputed matters.

o: things left to conscience, not commanded or forbidden
church rules that only the clergy have to keep
sins so small that God simply overlooks them

games.q: what's inside the word — tap the pairs.
p: a small cross on the wrist

s: the Bible names gambling as a sin
it never names it. churches reason from other texts, and they disagree.
Paul told the Romans to settle every holy-day question for each other
he said: "Let every man be fully persuaded in his own mind."
some churches serve grape juice at communion instead of wine
many Baptist, Pentecostal and Methodist churches do; Catholics, Orthodox, Lutherans and Anglicans use wine.

games.q: at dinner, one cousin says tattoos are a sin. another shows off a new one. both look at you. where does Paul's advice point?
o: pick a side and win the argument.
say what you think, and don't judge the one who differs.
games.why: "judge this rather, that no man put a stumblingblock" in his brother's way. be persuaded, and be kind.

practice: Bring to mind one is-it-a-sin question you've carried, about yourself or someone you love. Don't answer it; just notice how it sits in your body: tight, guilty, curious, annoyed.
Then picture someone you respect who lands on the other side of it. If you pray, ask for a clear conscience and a kind heart; if you don't, let the question rest without a verdict.

wordCard.voice: Adiaphora: things indifferent, matters left to conscience, where sincere Christians land in different places.

carryVoice: Your line: be persuaded, and be kind. Allowed isn't always helpful. Day one hundred twenty-three.
